question: What distinguishes the body from other supports established by consciousness?
premises: The body has a distinction: it functions as the prior support for all other things established.
Other things operate through identity with that bodily support.
Even though this is so, that dependence is not ordinarily recognized.
inference: The body is uniquely primary among supports, yet its foundational role usually remains unnoticed.
plain_english: The body has this distinction: it is the prior support for all else. Although other things function through identity with it, that is not recognized even when it is present.
